concept: participant recruitment for a post-stroke gait rehabilitation study using a wearable robotic exoskeleton

children.description: Specify stroke type, lesion location or laterality, time since stroke, and clinical stability requirements for inclusion.
children.name: Define stroke-related eligibility criteria

children.description: Specify whether participants must walk independently, with supervision, or with an assistive device, including minimum distance or duration.
children.name: Define minimum walking ability

children.description: Set allowable or required values for walking speed, cadence, endurance, balance, and gait asymmetry relevant to exoskeleton training.
children.name: Specify gait-performance limits

children.description: Identify mobility conditions that could make assisted walking unsafe, such as inability to maintain standing balance or excessive fall risk.
children.name: Define safety-related mobility criteria

children.description: Establish acceptable walking ability, lower-limb motor impairment, balance capacity, assistive-device use, and functional assessment thresholds.
children.name: Set ambulatory and motor-function requirements

children.description: Identify physical, orthopedic, neurological, cognitive, and cardiovascular criteria affecting safe use and compatibility with the wearable robotic exoskeleton.
children.name: Screen exoskeleton safety and fit factors

children.description: Set target ranges for age, sex, stroke representation, and geographic or clinical-site distribution to support the intended study population.
children.name: Define recruitment demographics and site coverage

children.description: The clinical, demographic, functional, and safety characteristics defining who the study is intended to recruit.
children.name: Target participant population

children.description: Identify stroke centers, rehabilitation hospitals, outpatient clinics, neurologists, physiatrists, and physical therapists that can refer potentially eligible participants.
children.name: Map clinical referral sources

children.description: Engage stroke survivor organizations, support groups, community rehabilitation programs, and local advocacy networks to reach individuals outside formal clinical pathways.
children.name: Establish community outreach channels

children.description: Create and distribute accessible flyers, email announcements, social media posts, registry notices, and study webpages explaining the exoskeleton intervention and eligibility screening process.
children.name: Deploy participant-facing recruitment materials

children.description: Track inquiries, screened candidates, enrollments, referral volume, and participant demographics by recruitment source and location to identify gaps and redirect outreach.
children.name: Monitor source performance and geographic reach

children.description: The settings, networks, channels, and geographic scope through which eligible potential participants can be identified and accessed.
children.name: Recruitment sources and reach

children.description: Set the required sample size, recruitment timeline, eligibility profile, and feasible referral channels such as stroke clinics, rehabilitation centers, registries, and community organizations.
children.name: Define enrollment targets and recruitment sources

children.description: Create accessible advertisements, invitations, and informational materials explaining the study purpose, exoskeleton experience, time commitment, eligibility, compensation, and contact process.
children.name: Develop participant-facing recruitment materials

children.description: Specify stroke-related, functional, medical, cognitive, and safety criteria for inclusion and exclusion.
children.name: Define eligibility criteria

children.description: Develop a standardized method for reviewing referrals, medical records, or prescreening questionnaires against the eligibility criteria.
children.name: Create the initial screening process

children.description: Use consistent assessments to verify gait ability, mobility level, physical capacity, and contraindications to wearable exoskeleton use.
children.name: Conduct standardized eligibility assessments

children.description: Record eligibility determinations, reasons for exclusion, pending information, and appropriate follow-up or referral actions.
children.name: Document screening decisions and referrals

children.description: Implement referral intake, prescreening, clinical eligibility checks, mobility and safety assessments, and standardized tracking of screening outcomes and reasons for exclusion.
children.name: Establish screening and eligibility workflows

children.description: Monitor reasons for declining or withdrawing, gather feedback on comfort and perceived burden, and adjust scheduling, transportation, caregiver support, communication, and onboarding procedures to improve acceptability.
children.name: Assess participation barriers and refine the enrollment process

children.description: The factors influencing willingness and ability to participate, including perceived relevance, burden, accessibility, trust, and retention potential.
children.name: Enrollment feasibility and acceptability

root.name: participant recruitment for a post-stroke gait rehabilitation study using a wearable robotic exoskeleton
